themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 8 THIS WEEK, up 1180% from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.43), signaling either a sudden proliferation of unlicensed vendors or a coordinated enforcement/complaint push in Greenpoint-Williamsburg.
evidence: 8 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (1180% spike)
Z-score of 7.43 indicates statistically extreme deviation
No prior week in 8-week baseline exceeded 2 complaints
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors clustering in specific parks or commercial corridors (e.g., Domino Park, waterfront)?
Has the city recently launched a crackdown or increased enforcement in CD 301?

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK, a 224% increase from the 4.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.27), suggesting a spike in low-level crime reports, quality-of-life issues, or public order disturbances.
evidence: 15 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average (224% spike)
Z-score of 6.27 indicates highly significant statistical deviation
Timing coincides with public safety concerns reflected in Gothamist coverage of East Williamsburg shooting (April 4)
reporting_angles: What specific quality-of-life or low-level crime issues are driving the spike (e.g., street harassment, trespassing, disorderly conduct)?
Is there spatial clustering in East Williamsburg or other neighborhoods within CD 301?
Are residents responding to recent high-profile crime (baby girl shooting) with heightened vigilance?

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Skyrocket
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about violation of park rules surged to 4 LAST WEEK, a 1500% spike from the 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66, highest statistical severity in dataset), pointing to either new park enforcement, a specific incident, or emerging misuse patterns in Greenpoint parks.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike)
Highest z-score in entire dataset at 8.66, indicating most extreme statistical anomaly
Brooklyn Eagle article on 'I Love My Park Day' (April 3) suggests heightened park engagement and possible scrutiny
reporting_angles: Which parks are generating complaints (Domino Park, McGolrick Park, waterfront parks)?
What violations are being reported: off-leash dogs, after-hours use, vendor activity, trespassing?
Is Parks Dept. enforcement being ramped up, or are residents increasingly reporting violations?

themes_detail.label: Sewage & Sewer Infrastructure Issues
themes_detail.summary: Indoor sewage complaints and root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints combined represent 700-233% spikes over 8-week baselines (3 and 5 complaints respectively, z-scores 5.42 and 4.95), suggesting emerging basement flooding, sewer backups, or subsurface infrastructure failures in the district.
evidence: Indoor sewage complaints: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 5 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average (233% spike, z-score 4.95)
Community board budget requests include repeated 'Other capital budget request for DEP' — chronic infrastructure concern
reporting_angles: Are basement flooding or sewer backups concentrated in specific neighborhoods (low-lying areas near waterfront)?
Is aging infrastructure in Greenpoint-Williamsburg (historic industrial district) reaching failure point?
Has DEP conducted recent maintenance or identified problem areas?

themes_detail.label: Lost Property Reports Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Lost property complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 380% increase from the 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.91), potentially indicating theft, package theft, or bike theft clusters that warrant investigation.
evidence: 3 lost property complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (380% spike, z-score 4.91)
Timing aligns with broader public safety spike (non-emergency police complaints up 224% this week)
Low historical baseline suggests this is newly emerging pattern, not endemic issue
reporting_angles: What types of property are being reported lost (packages, bicycles, personal items)?
Is there spatial clustering (e.g., specific subway stations, residential blocks)?
Are residents frustrated with police response or recovery prospects?
